title: Welcome to Our Growing DigiGreenTT Group Network
excerpt: FITTER-EU welcomes ten new DigiGreenTT Group to our network, expanding opportunities for cross-project collaboration on fair transitions.
content:
We are delighted to welcome ten Horizon Europe projects to the FITTER-EU DigigreenTT Project Network. This diverse group brings expertise across just transition, digital inclusion, green skills, and policy development.

## New Network Members

Our network now includes projects such as, ST4TE, Greenpaths, Twin Synergies, and others who share our commitment to ensuring Europe's twin transition is fair and inclusive for all.

## Collaboration Opportunities

With this expanded network, we see significant opportunities for:

- Cross-project knowledge exchange on methodologies and tools
- Joint stakeholder engagement activities
- Collaborative publications addressing common challenges
- Shared dissemination and outreach

## Join Us

If your Horizon Europe project works on related themes and you'd like to join our network, visit the Collaborate page to apply.

## Learn More

Visit the Sister Projects page to explore the full network and learn about each project's focus and activities.

title: FITTER-EU Launches DigiGreenTT Group Engagement Platform
excerpt: A new dedicated platform for cross-project collaboration between Horizon Europe projects working on fair twin transitions is now live.
content:
We are pleased to announce the launch of the FITTER-EU initiated DigiGreenTT Group Engagement platform, designed to facilitate collaboration and knowledge sharing between Horizon Europe projects focused on fair, inclusive green and digital transitions.

## Purpose

The platform serves as a central hub for:

- Connecting projects with complementary expertise
- Proposing and coordinating joint activities
- Sharing resources and best practices
- Building a community of practice around just transitions.

## Get Involved

Projects working on related themes are invited to join our network and explore collaboration opportunities. Visit the Collaborate page to submit your project or propose a joint activity.

## Contact

For more information, contact the FITTER-EU team at contact@tfcengage.com .

title: DigiGreenTT Welcomes Prof. Christina Kakderi
excerpt: We are delighted to  welcome  Prof. Kakderi as the first speaker for our autumn webinar series. Prof. Christina Kakderi,  is the coordinator of the ST4TE & PACT projects, joins us on 9th Sept 26 to present the #dashboard and #API built by ST4TE for the just measuring of the #twintransition.
content:
Christina is Associate Professor at the School of Spatial Planning and Development, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (AUTH), Greece, and a member of the URENIO Research Unit. Her research primarily focuses on regional innovation systems, smart cities, innovation policy, regional resilience, and the green, digital and twin transitions and it is the latter that the DigiGreenTT cluster webinar will focus on.

Christina coordinates the HorizonEurope project ST4TE (Strategies for Just and Equitable Twin Transitions in Europe) and the Horizon Europe project PACT. Both examine how Europe's transitions can be made more inclusive and territorially balanced, which is of importance across many regions of Europe. Her recent research focuses on measuring regional green, digital and twin transitions and examining their implications for regional development and territorial cohesion and the webinar centred on this. 

It promises to be insightful!

DigiGreenTT webinar:
🗓️ 9th September 2026 │ 15:00–16:00 CET

https://lnkd.in/d-i4ZSGK

title: FITTER-EU Final Conference
excerpt: "From Insight to impact: Innovating for an Inclusive Twin Transition in Europe"
content:
Registration is open for Fitter-EU Final Conference

"From Insight to impact: Innovating for an Inclusive Twin Transition in Europe"

Registration link: https://lnkd.in/d7DJ5eph

Fitter-EU's final event brings together policymakers, researchers and practitioners for a day of discussion on the project's findings and what should happen next.

Since 2024, the project has been researching how Europe's green and digital transitions play out across different regions, sectors and groups, and what it would take for the benefits to reach further than they currently do. In Seville, we set out what that research shows and open it up for discussion.

The day is designed for exchange rather than presentation, so there will be time to question the conclusions and bring your own experience into the conversation.

📅 26 November 2026
📍 JRC Seville, Spain

Register today to secure your place.

title: Leaving No One Behind
excerpt:
"Shaping green and digital transition policies that work
for all people and territories in Europe"
content: The ST4TE Final Conference will examine how EU, national, regional and local policy can respond to the uneven pathways of the twin transition. Drawing on new evidence on technological specialisation, employment, skills, income, health and regional vulnerability, the conference will consider where existing policy instruments are working, where significant gaps remain, and how support can be better targeted at the people and places most at risk of being left behind. The conference will also launch ST4TE's Twin Transition Inequalities Index and its accompanying regional dashboard, and present the policy recommendations set out in the project's White Paper. Sessions will bring together policymakers and officials from EU institutions and from national, regional and local levels, alongside researchers, civil society representatives, social partners and sister Horizon Europe projects. Read the newly published Territorial Impact Assessment Report on Regional Skills Partnerships for insights into how twin transition policies affect European regions. For further information on the agenda please use the link below: ST4TE Final Conference | ST4TE?

title: DigiGreenTT Cluster - Green & Digital Transition Webinar Series 1
excerpt: On 9th September, the DigiGreenTT cluster webinar was held.
content:
Titled "Beyond Green and Digital: 
Rethinking the Measurement of the Twin Transition" - a look at how the twin transition is measured across European regions, it was presented by Dr. Christina Kakderi (AUTH, ST4TE) and moderated by Mary Corbett (TFC, FITTER-EU). It is primarily based on the work and findings of the ongoing #HorizonEurope ST4TE project.

Dr. Karderi explained digital technologies are meant to reinforce each other, with digital tools making green solutions smarter and more controllable, while green objectives give digital technologies a purpose beyond efficiency alone. She illustrated this, sector by sector for instance, renewable energy generation combined with grid sensing and control produces smart grids capable of balancing intermittent supply; electrification combined with connectivity enables lower-emission connected mobility. The central question of the session was deceptively simple: is that combination actually happening and where, and for whom?

title: Driving the Green and Digital Transitions
excerpt: Showcasing five projects at the Fitter-EU Final Conference!
content:
We are pleased to highlight an exciting opportunity for the DigiGreenTT members at the upcoming Fitter-EU Final Conference, taking place on 26 November 2026 at the Joint Research Centre (JRC) in Seville, Spain.

As Europe continues to navigate the twin transition, the interconnected green and digital transformations are reshaping industries, skills, education, and the future of work. While digitalisation creates opportunities for innovation, efficiency, and connectivity, the green transition calls for more sustainable practices, responsible resource use, and climate-conscious solutions. Addressing these two transitions together is essential to building a more sustainable, inclusive, and competitive future.

As part of the conference, a dedicated poster presentation session will provide DigiGreenTT members with an opportunity to showcase their projects, share their experiences, and discuss how their initiatives are tackling the challenges of the twin transition.

Meet the projects contributing to the twin transition:

  • 🔹 YCONIC
  • 🔹 GreenPaths
  • 🔹 ESIRA
  • 🔹 Genesys
  • 🔹 ST4TE

Through this poster session, the projects will have a platform to present their work, highlight their approaches, and exchange ideas on the opportunities and challenges of combining digital innovation with environmental sustainability.

The session will also encourage dialogue, knowledge sharing, and collaboration among researchers, practitioners, stakeholders, and other participants working towards a greener and more digital Europe. By bringing these initiatives together, the conference offers an opportunity to explore different perspectives, share lessons learned, and identify potential synergies that can help accelerate the twin transition.

Why does the twin transition matter?

The twin transition is not simply about adopting new technologies or reducing environmental impact independently. It is about understanding how digital and green solutions can complement one another while ensuring that the transition remains practical, inclusive, and responsive to the needs of people, organisations, and communities.

The contributions of the DigiGreenTT members will bring these discussions to life by showcasing project experiences, innovative approaches, and insights that can inform wider conversations about sustainability, digital transformation, and future-ready skills.

Date: 26 November 2026

Venue: Joint Research Centre (JRC), Seville, Spain

Event: Fitter-EU Final Conference

Highlight: Poster presentations by DigiGreenTT members

We look forward to seeing these projects represented, learning more about their work, and connecting with others committed to advancing the green and digital transitions across Europe.

Together, let's share knowledge, strengthen collaboration, and contribute to a more sustainable and digitally empowered future!

title: Tackling Inequalities in the Green and Digital Transitions: Three EU Projects Collaborate on a New Policy White Paper
excerpt: The green and digital transitions are transforming Europe, creating new opportunities while raising important questions about equality, inclusion. How can these transitions be made fairer, ensuring that their benefits reach everyone?
content:
To explore this question, three EU projects, ST4TE, FITTER-EU, and READJUST, are contributing to a joint policy white paper titled ‘Tackling Inequalities in the Green and Digital Transitions’. By bringing together their respective project experiences and expertise, the initiatives aim to develop policy recommendations that address inequalities and support more inclusive transitions across Europe.

A shared effort, three project perspectives

The first coordination meeting brought representatives from all three projects together to discuss the white paper’s content, development process, and the role each project will play in shaping the publication.

The meeting marked the beginning of a collaborative effort to bring together the projects’ distinct experiences and insights. By drawing on their respective contributions, the white paper will explore inequalities associated with the green and digital transitions and identify ways to address them through policy.

The meeting was attended by:

  • ST4TE: Christina Kakderi, Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
  • FITTER-EU: Tom Flynn, TFC; Sara Clavero, TU Dublin; and Sushmita Puhan, TFC
  • READJUST: Hannia Karime Gonzalez Urango, YAGHMA

The representatives discussed how to coordinate their contributions and establish a shared direction for the white paper, while ensuring that each project’s specific experience is reflected in the final publication.

From collaboration to policy action

By bringing together insights from three distinct projects, the white paper aims to connect project experience with wider policy discussions on equality and inclusion. Its recommendations will seek to inform efforts to ensure that the benefits of Europe’s green and digital transitions are shared more fairly.

The initial meeting laid the foundation for this joint effort, bringing ST4TE, FITTER-EU, and READJUST together around a common goal: helping shape green and digital transitions that are more inclusive and equitable for all.
